timeline_disposition.reason: Sakya Paṇḍita (1182–1251) is a securely historical Tibetan philosopher and Sakya scholar, but the reviewed evidence spans monastic, intellectual, and later Mongol-court contexts rather than one defensible canonical polity interval for his philosophical activity. ATLAS therefore preserves the historical Person without manufacturing a single polity-bound Activity rail.

sources.title: Sakya Paṇḍita — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.citation_text: SEP identifies Sakya Paṇḍita (1182–1251) as a major Tibetan philosopher, especially influential in epistemology, philosophy of language, debate, grammar, lexicography and poetics.

sources.title: Sakya Paṇḍita Kunga Gyeltsen — The Treasury of Lives
sources.citation_text: The Treasury of Lives records Sakya Paṇḍita Kunga Gyeltsen as a historical Tibetan scholar, 1182–1251, associated with Sakya Monastery and serving as the sixth Sakya Trizin.

review_context.namuwiki_review: Exact indexed searches for 사캬 판디타/사키야 판디타/사꺄 빤디따 and Sakya Pandita returned no independent NamuWiki Person document; no guessed URL.
review_context.timeline_decision: Secure historical identity and life dates retained; no single polity rail forced across distinct Tibetan monastic/intellectual and later Mongol-court contexts.
